content:
sam: heads-up — ran into a weird perf regression after a driver restart: some requests are hitting slow kernel paths for short sequences. guessing stale cache entries + kernel-autotune mismatch.

maria: can you paste the repro? which model + seqlen bins?

sam: repro is on rwd-gpt-7b, load pattern mostly <=64 but with a small tail 256+. after driver restart we saw ~2x token latency for <=64. profiler points to fallback to matmul kernel instead of fused attention for seqlen bin 32.

chen: hmm, did the driver change the kernel-selection policy id? we recently shipped kernel-selector v3 that changes how we hash kernel signatures.

sam: yes — driver rolled with selector v3 ~12:10. cache persistence uses key schema: 
```
model:{model_id}:kv_cache:{seqlen_bin}:{kernel_sig}
```
but kernel_sig used to be `arch+layout+fuse_flags` and now includes `selector_version` in the in-memory path only, not in persisted keys. result: persisted keys map to wrong kernels after selector bump.

alex: oh that explains it. so the runtime loaded persisted entries whose kernel_sig didn't include selector_version, then selector v3 expects different kernels -> compatibility mismatch -> fallback slow path.

julie: possible fixes: 1) include selector_version in persisted key (breaking change, needs migration), 2) invalidate all persisted cache on selector rollout, 3) add a compatibility layer that maps old sigs to new ones.

maria: we should also consider graceful rollout: when rolling selector, mark new driver instances to ignore persisted keys until they reach a checkpoint that re-warms the cache. maybe a per-driver durability flag.

sam: i prototyped a cheap invalidation hook: driver writes a header file /var/lib/redwood/selector_version and KV loader compares. if mismatch => skip persistence load. quick but fragile for private deployments.

infra-bot: deploy event: kernel-selector v3 rolled to infra pool-a at 2025-11-02T12:10:32Z (noticed by health-check).

chen: opt-by-default: i think canonical solution is to encode selection graph version into the persisted key and bump on any selector codepath change. we also need to set a TTL for persisted entries to prevent long-lived mismatch.

alex: TTL alone won't help immediate rollout. we should add an explicit invalidation epoch. store `model:{id}:cache_epoch` in central metadata service; on driver startup compare. if epoch mismatch then delete persisted keys or mark stale.

sam: performance numbers from experiment: baseline pre-rolling (warm cache): p50 token-latency 10ms, p95 22ms. after roll with stale persisted keys: p50 18ms, p95 48ms. re-warming by forcing invalidation restored to baseline in ~30 min.

julie: noted. also watch out for multi-tenant persistence: some customers use shared persistence; invalidation must be scoped to model+pool, not global.

maria: for the short term i propose:
- patch runtime to include `selector_version` in persisted key (backfill plan: keep old keys valid for 2 weeks)
- add cache_epoch metadata and an admin API to bump epoch on major driver changes
- add a smoke-check in deploy pipeline that runs a quick seqlen-profile after rollout and auto-roll back if p95 regresses >20%

chen: agree. i'll own the persisted-key patch. alex can you do cache_epoch service and admin API?

alex: yep. i'll also add a migration flag to the loader so operators can force re-warm.

sam: i'll prepare a short repro script + a dashboard widget for the seqlen breakdown and kernel hit-rate. will post link once ready.

infra-bot: alert: rollout smoke-check failed for pool-a: p95 45ms (>20% threshold). tagging @oncall-eng-runtime.

julie: thanks. oncall please pause further selector rollouts until we have the key-versioning fix in staging. :no_entry_sign:

chen: timeline: i'll open PR for key schema change today (ETA 1d), alex will have cache_epoch API (ETA 2d), sam will provide repro/metrics (ETA EOD). then we run canary in staging.

maria: 👍 keep thread updated.

sam: quick repro snippet for stress:
```
# run short seq load + occasional long tails
wrk -t4 -c200 -d600s --script seqlen_mixture.lua --server https://rwd-infer/internal
```
seqlen_mixture.lua contains a mix of 90% seq<=64, 10% seq=256.

alex: also instrument loader to emit what key formats were seen during startup (old vs new). helps postmortem.

sam: yep added that. last note: document decision in runtime README and add a migration playbook for enterprise/private customers (they might not want forced invalidation without notice).

maria: perfect. thanks team.

sam: will follow up with PR links and dashboard.
